title: AgentReady Lab finding message templates v0
description: The static message templates ADR-0002 section 6 requires, keyed by assertion id and outcome kind. A rule may not construct a message: it reports an outcome kind and typed parameters, and packages/core/src/engine/render-message.ts renders the prose from this table. Template text is fixed and target-independent; the only value that can vary is a declared parameter of the assertion, which the core sanitizes and bounds before substitution. It is a separate file from the ruleset for the reason remediation is: it declares no assertion, pins no source, and changes when a human rewrites prose rather than when behaviour changes.

templates_version.description: This table's own version axis, moving when the prose changes and not when a rule does. It decides no verdict, so it carries no digest, for the reason remediation_version carries none.

ruleset_id.description: The ruleset whose assertion ids these keys are. Held equal to specs/ruleset.standard.v0.yaml's by the validator, because a version recorded in one file and never compared with the other is decoration.

ruleset_version.description: The ruleset_version these templates were written against, held equal to the ruleset's.

todo.description: Values an accepted decision requires but does not supply, and open items about this table. Printed by the validator as a listed note, never as an error.

entry.description: One assertion's four templates. Unique on `assertion` across the file.

assertion.description: ADR-0002 section 9: a spec.requirements id for a spec-mode assertion, or the rule's own versioned compatibility assertion id for a compat-mode one. Both shapes are accepted, as in specs/remediation.schema.json.

rule_id.description: The rule that declares the assertion. Carried so a reader of this file alone can tell which rule a template belongs to; the validator holds it equal to the ruleset's.

messages.description: One template per outcome kind of packages/core/src/model/status.ts. All four are required rather than only the kinds the current rule body happens to reach, because renderMessage throws missing-message-template on a kind it has no entry for and no file can tell which kinds a compiled rule produces. Which kinds a rule version does not currently reach is recorded in that entry's `todo`.

template.description: Static prose with typed parameter slots. A slot is {name} naming a parameter the assertion declares in specs/ruleset.standard.v0.yaml; the validator rejects any other name, and renderMessage substitutes the sanitized, bounded value. No other part of the string may vary, so no target-controlled byte can reach a report except through a declared parameter. The 320-character cap sits under the 512-character message cap in packages/reporters/src/sanitize.ts, so a rendered message carrying one count parameter is never truncated by the human reporter.
